member.name: F:MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.Models.NumericalMethods.RootFindingAlgorithm.BisectionMethod
member.summary: The Bisection method is a root-finding algorithm for a continuous function within a given interval. It works by repeatedly dividing the interval in half and narrowing down the search range until a sufficiently accurate approximation of the root is found.

member.name: F:MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.Models.NumericalMethods.RootFindingAlgorithm.BrentMethod
member.summary: Brent's method is a hybrid root-finding algorithm combining the bisection method, the secant method and inverse quadratic interpolation. The algorithm tries to use the potentially fast-converging secant method or inverse quadratic interpolation if possible, it falls back to the more robust bisection method if necessary.

member.summary: Advances the dynamic system by one time step, computing the state (displacement, velocity, acceleration and equivalent force) at the requested instant .
member.param: The system data: time step Δt (s), mass matrix [M] (kg), stiffness matrix [K] (N/m), damping matrix [C] (N·s/m), the equivalent force vector at (N) and the number of boundary conditions. Δt is read from input.TimeStep and must be consistent across calls so that the integration constants remain valid.
The current instant, in seconds, at which the result must be evaluated. Must be greater than or equal to the configured initial time.
The state at the previous instant time − Δt. Must not be for any step beyond the initial one. At the initial instant the implementation returns the initial state directly and ignores this argument.
member.returns: The numerical state of the system at .
member.remarks: Implementations integrate a second-order ODE of the form [M]ẍ + [C]ẋ + [K]x = F(t). The classic uses γ = 1/2, β = 1/4 (constant-average-acceleration) which is unconditionally stable and second-order accurate. The variant uses γ = 1/2, β = 1/6 (linear-acceleration), which is conditionally stable (Δt must be small relative to the highest natural period) but provides better phase accuracy.
